subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw-hooks helper processes orphaned when a run terminates abnormally

question: Should abnormal relay-tree cleanup be owned in OpenClaw's Codex integration, in the Codex helper runtime, or through a coordinated contract across both?
rationale: The report is credible, but process ownership and safe termination semantics span the OpenClaw integration and the Codex runtime; source-level normal cleanup alone does not determine the correct boundary.

options.title: Assign the OpenClaw integration boundary
options.body: Make the Codex integration own relay process-group supervision and require a current-version abnormal-termination regression test.

options.title: Escalate to Codex runtime ownership
options.body: Treat helper parent-death behavior as a Codex runtime contract and coordinate an upstream fix before changing OpenClaw lifecycle code.

options.title: Define a shared contract first
options.body: Specify parent, child, restart, and timeout responsibilities across both layers before choosing the implementation owner.

recommendation.title: Assign the OpenClaw integration boundary
recommendation.body: Make the Codex integration own relay process-group supervision and require a current-version abnormal-termination regression test.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent native-hook lifecycle work makes joshavant the strongest available routing candidate for deciding the OpenClaw-side boundary.
